# symbolicVariableScopeTest.py

You can view and download this file on Github: [symbolicVariableScopeTest.py](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/tree/master/python/TestModels/symbolicVariableScopeTest.py)

```{code-block} python
:linenos:

#+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
# This is an EXUDYN example
#
# Details:  The scopes of the named symbolic variables (#3208): esym.Real(name, value, scope=mbs) gives the variable of
#           that name in mbs.symbolicVariables, the scope of the model - a new one, or the one there with the value
#           set -; without scope the variable of esym.variables. A symbolic user function reads only its arguments and
#           the variables of mbs.symbolicVariables, at every call; one of esym.variables and a named variable created
#           while recording are refused. mbs.Reset() empties the scope, GetDictionary and SetDictionary keep it.
#           exudyn.special.deprecations.symbolicVariablesWithoutScope restores the variables of no scope.
#
# Author:   Johannes Gerstmayr
# Date:     2026-11-02
#
# Copyright:This file is part of Exudyn. Exudyn is free software. You can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the Exudyn license. See 'LICENSE.txt' for more details.
#
#+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

import exudyn as exu
from exudyn.utilities import * #includes itemInterface and rigidBodyUtilities

esym = exu.symbolic

def Raises(function, exceptionType):
    try:
        function()
    except exceptionType:
        return 1
    return 0

SC = exu.SystemContainer()
mbs = SC.AddSystem()
failed = 0

#the model's scope: one variable per name, the second call sets its value
k = esym.Real('k', 100., scope=mbs)
kAgain = esym.Real('k', 200., scope=mbs)
failed += int(k.Evaluate() != 200. or mbs.symbolicVariables.GetNames() != ['k'])
v = esym.Vector('offset', [0.1, 0.2], scope=mbs)
failed += int(mbs.symbolicVariables.GetNames() != ['k', 'offset'])
#a name of another kind replaces the variable
esym.Vector('offset', [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], scope=mbs)
failed += int(len(mbs.symbolicVariables.Get('offset').Evaluate()) != 3)

#the global scope esym.variables, the same way
x = esym.Real('symbolicVariableScopeTestX', 1.)
failed += int(not esym.variables.Exists('symbolicVariableScopeTestX'))
failed += int(esym.Real('symbolicVariableScopeTestX', 3.).Evaluate() != 3. or x.Evaluate() != 3.)

#a spring-damper whose stiffness is the variable k of the model, read at every call
ground = mbs.CreateGround()
mass = mbs.CreateMassPoint(referencePosition=[1, 0, 0], mass=1)
def SpringForce(mbs, t, itemNumber, deltaL, deltaL_t, stiffness, damping, force):
    return mbs.symbolicVariables.Get('k')*deltaL + damping*deltaL_t
symbolicForce = CreateSymbolicUserFunction(mbs, SpringForce, 'springForceUserFunction', itemTypeName='ObjectConnectorSpringDamper')
mbs.CreateSpringDamper(itemNumbers=[ground, mass], referenceLength=1, stiffness=0, damping=1,
                       springForceUserFunction=symbolicForce)
args = (0., 0, 0.1, 0., 0., 1., 0.)
failed += int(symbolicForce.Evaluate(mbs, *args) != 20.)
k.SetValue(50.)
failed += int(symbolicForce.Evaluate(mbs, *args) != 5.)

#refused: a variable of esym.variables, a named variable created while recording
def ReadsGlobal(mbs, t, itemNumber, deltaL, deltaL_t, stiffness, damping, force):
    return x*deltaL
failed += 1 - Raises(lambda: CreateSymbolicUserFunction(mbs, ReadsGlobal, 'springForceUserFunction',
                                                        itemTypeName='ObjectConnectorSpringDamper'), ValueError)
def CreatesVariable(mbs, t, itemNumber, deltaL, deltaL_t, stiffness, damping, force):
    return esym.Real('c', 1., scope=mbs)*deltaL
failed += 1 - Raises(lambda: CreateSymbolicUserFunction(mbs, CreatesVariable, 'springForceUserFunction',
                                                        itemTypeName='ObjectConnectorSpringDamper'), ValueError)
failed += 1 - Raises(lambda: esym.Real('k', 1., scope=3), TypeError) #a scope must be None, a MainSystem or a VariableSet

#Reset empties the scope; the dictionary of a system keeps it
mbs.Reset()
failed += int(mbs.symbolicVariables.NumberOfItems() != 0)
esym.Real('k', 50., scope=mbs)
esym.Vector('offset', [0.1, 0.2], scope=mbs)
mbs2 = SC.AddSystem()
mbs2.SetDictionary(mbs.GetDictionary())
failed += int(mbs2.symbolicVariables.GetNames() != ['k', 'offset'] or mbs2.symbolicVariables.Get('k').Evaluate() != 50.)

#the old behaviour: two variables of one name, and a user function may read any named variable
exu.special.deprecations.symbolicVariablesWithoutScope = True
a0 = esym.Real('a', 1.)
a1 = esym.Real('a', 2.)
failed += int(a0.Evaluate() != 1. or a1.Evaluate() != 2.)
mbs3 = SC.AddSystem()
CreateSymbolicUserFunction(mbs3, ReadsGlobal, 'springForceUserFunction', itemTypeName='ObjectConnectorSpringDamper')
exu.special.deprecations.symbolicVariablesWithoutScope = False

u = failed
exu.Print('solution of symbolicVariableScopeTest=', u)
exu.sys['testResult'] = u
```
